requirements.title: Enterprise admin means company-wide super-admin
requirements.statement: In first-project onboarding, "enterprise admin" means company-wide super-admin. It does not mean regional admin or project admin.

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

acceptance_criteria.given: Track3D onboards a customer and invites their enterprise admin
acceptance_criteria.then: That person holds company-wide super-admin for their company, not a regional or project admin role

requirements.title: Company super-admins can create projects
requirements.statement: Company-wide super-admins can create additional projects. Exceptions, delegated permissions and cross-company scope are not defined.

requirements.title: Regions group projects and carry authority
requirements.statement: A region has a name that is unique within its company. Creating one assigns its projects to it and grants regional authority to the chosen users and to the company's super-admins. Changing a region changes who can act on its projects; it is more than a label.

acceptance_criteria.given: Company C already has a region named West
acceptance_criteria.when: Someone creates another region named " West " in C
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected as a duplicate

requirements.title: Removing a user from a project removes all their grants there
requirements.statement: A company super-admin, or the regional admin of the project's region, can remove a user from a project. This deletes the user's direct role and every group-derived grant on that project. Their group membership is unchanged, so a later group update can grant the access again.
open_checks: The project lookup omits the region field the regional-admin check reads

acceptance_criteria.given: A user with a direct viewer role on P who is also in group G granting collaborator on P
acceptance_criteria.when: A company super-admin removes them from P
acceptance_criteria.then: They lose all access to P but remain a member of G

requirements.title: Removing users from a company deactivates them everywhere
requirements.statement: Removing users from a company skips the person doing the removal and any company super-admin. Each removed user is deactivated and anonymised and loses every role assignment, including in other companies' projects. Their sessions are revoked after the change is saved.
open_checks: Company, header, linked-company, project and group scope are not traced through parent mounts and controllers; several route permission calls are commented out (T3D-IMPL-129)

acceptance_criteria.given: A super-admin removes themselves, another super-admin and an ordinary user from the company
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the ordinary user is removed, and the two super-admins are reported as skipped

acceptance_criteria.given: A removed user who was also a member of a linked company's project
acceptance_criteria.when: They are removed from their home company
acceptance_criteria.then: (Current behaviour) They lose access to that linked project too

requirements.title: Enterprise invitations validate domains and expire after 2 days
requirements.statement: Invited emails are trimmed, lower-cased and de-duplicated. An existing user from a linked company can be assigned directly; any other existing user is rejected. A new email must be on the company's or a linked company's domain. Invitations expire after 2 days by default. Resending renews an expired one, and an unexpired pending invitation isn't sent again.
open_checks: The reported "sent" count is not delivery confirmation; the email call isn't awaited

acceptance_criteria.given: Company A, linked to B, invites " Jo@B.com " and kim@gmail.com
acceptance_criteria.then: jo@b.com is accepted (normalised) and kim@gmail.com is rejected for its domain

acceptance_criteria.given: An enterprise invitation sent three days ago and never accepted
acceptance_criteria.then: It shows as expired, and resending creates a renewed invitation
